name: momentum-weak
description: T-022 operator packet, run B of two: the SAME build and the SAME URL (index.html?momentum=1) played BADLY, so the pair differ only in how they are played. The policy is a player who has not learned the game yet — it only moves when the damage plane crowds it (edgeMargin<12), never aims up, and jumps only at the lip it is about to walk off. That keeps RIG on the LEFT of the screen, where decisions.md entry 11's daylight bank is empty: below CONFIG.momentum.bankLo (0.55 of the strip) the bank term is EXACTLY zero, so the only escalation left to a struggling player is the combat term, and its whole authority is wCombat = 0.3 of the range. FALSIFYING GATE, stated in what the code guarantees rather than in a raw speed: read `pursuitSpeed` out of `report.json` -> `trace` (the per-sample array; the report has no `samples` key) and convert with drive = (pursuitSpeed/4.3 - 1)/0.4. (1) If drive ever exceeds 0.30 — pursuitSpeed above 4.82 t/s, x1.12 — the bank deadband leaked and a player being carried was escalated at on daylight he never banked: the floor promise is broken and the task is not done. (2) After a hit, drive must be at or below hitDrive 0.35 (4.90 t/s) on the frame it lands and must not rise again for 1500 ms. (3) After a lost life the trace must return to exactly 4.30. Escalation from KILLS inside that x1.12 bound is design-correct, not a failure — the combat term is independent of the bank by design, so a struggling player who holds fire and connects will read slightly above the floor. MEASURED, NOT ASPIRATIONAL — two runs on task/T-022's own tree (2026-08-01, --deterministic, 1440x900, `--max-runtime-ms 62000`; the 60 s window needs that cap raised off its 25000 ms default): 362 / 368 PLAYING samples; pursuitSpeed median exactly 4.300 (x1.00) both times, p90 4.31 / 4.39, peak 4.41 / 4.51 t/s (x1.02 / x1.05, drive 0.061 / 0.122) off the 5 / 6 kills a held fire button collected; above the floor on 11.6% / 24.2% of PLAYING samples and never once above the x1.12 bound. edgeMargin median 11.7 tiles both times against the strong run's 43.6-43.8, so the policy did sit where it was meant to. The 'pushed along while they learn' half is only PARTLY demonstrated here: RIG is conveyed forward to 75 m of scroll and then spends his last life at 27.5 / 27.9 s (GAME_OVER, SIGNAL LOST). This run shows the pace never escalated at a player who was losing; it does NOT by itself show that a struggling player can finish.
